newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Pertamina sees no fallout from Caltex field move.
newsitem.headline: Pertamina sees no fallout from Caltex field move.

text.p: Indonesian state oil company Pertamina said on Thursday its decision to take over a privately operated oil field when its contract expires would not affect investment in the sector.
Pertimina is due to take over the Coastal Plain Pakanbaru (CPP) oil block in central Sumatra from PT Caltex Pacific Indonesia in 2001.

"It is not true that oil investment will be affected. That opinion is exaggerated. We are going to sign some oil contracts in the near future," Pertamina president-director Faisal Abda'oe told reporters.
Pertamina exploration director Priyambodo Mulyosudirjo said seven oil contracts, mostly production sharing contracts, were currently awaiting approval by President Suharto.
Caltex, jointly owned by Chevron Corp and Texaco Inc, on Tuesday again appealed to the government to extend the 30-year contract after Pertamina earlier rejected a similar request.
Abda'oe said Pertamina had signed around 51 oil contracts in the past three years, including production-sharing contracts.

"We are confident the takeover of Caltex's CPP oil block will not affect oil investment in Indonesia. There is no clause in any oil contract that we should extend when it expires," Abda'oe said. "So it is our right to take it over."
The CPP block produces some 77,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude.

Caltex president director Baihaki Hakim said on Tuesday Caltex's total production in Indonesia was around 760,000 bpd, including 230,000 bpd from the Minas and 290,000 bpd from the Duri fields. Caltex's production comprises about half of Indonesia's total crude output.
